figure_inventory.description: The line '12/7 x 5/24 = (12 x 5)/(7 x 24)' in which the numerator factor 12 (top) and the denominator factor 24 (bottom) of the right-hand fraction are each enclosed in a black hand-drawn circle, to show that both have the common factor 12. Black ink on white.

The 12 in the numerator is struck through with a black diagonal line and has a small '1' written above it; the 24 in the denominator is struck through with a black diagonal line and has a small '2' written below it. Then '= (1 x 5)/(7 x 2) = 5/14'.

The expression '(14 x 25)/(15 x 42) = (1 x 5)/(3 x 3) = 5/9.' with the four numbers marked: 14 (numerator, left) is circled in BLACK, struck by a black diagonal line, with a black '1' above it; 42 (denominator, right) is circled in BLACK, struck by a black diagonal line, with a black '3' below it (14 and 42 are divided by 14: 1 and 3). 25 (numerator, right) is circled in RED, struck by a red diagonal line, with a red '5' above it; 15 (denominator, left) is circled in RED, struck by a red diagonal line, with a red '3' below it (25 and 15 are divided by 5: 5 and 3). A table with a red outline and red grid lines, 3 columns and 4 rows. The header row has a light salmon/pink fill with bold headings: 'Situation' | 'Multiplication' | 'Relationship'. Fractions are stacked (numerator over denominator). Body cells are white.

A unit square split into 4 rows and 2 columns = 8 equal cells (a wide rectangle shape: each cell wide and short). The top row (2 cells) is yellow with a thick black outline; its LEFT cell is blue-hatched and carries the label '1/8' (stacked, on a pale box) in the middle of the cell, its RIGHT cell is plain yellow. The 3 lower rows are white with grey lines. Above the left column a teal brace labelled '1/2' (stacked 1 over 2) spans the width of the left column (half of the square's width); at the left of the top row a teal brace labelled '1/4' spans the height of the top row (one quarter of the height). So the hatched rectangle is 1/2 wide and 1/4 tall = 1/8.

A unit square split into 2 rows and 4 columns = 8 equal cells (each cell tall and narrow). Above the left column a teal brace labelled '1/4' (stacked 1 over 4) spans the width of the left column (one quarter of the width); at the left of the top row a teal brace labelled '1/2' (stacked 1 over 2) spans the height of the top row (half of the height). A black arrow points straight down from the bottom of the rectangle to the word 'Answer'.

diagram.manim_description: Plain BG canvas, 16:9. Draw one horizontal ground line in INK from x = -6.0 to x = 6.0 at y = 0.6. Draw four identical saplings standing on the ground line at x = -4.5, x = -1.5, x = 1.5 and x = 4.5, left to right. Each sapling is a vertical INK stem from (x, 0.6) up to (x, 2.0) with two small leaf ellipses at the top, filled MARK_FILL with an INK outline, one leaning left and one leaning right. From the ground line at each of the four sapling x positions draw a dashed GUIDE vertical line down to y = -0.1. At y = -0.1 draw three double-headed INK arrows: from x = -4.5 to x = -1.5, from x = -1.5 to x = 1.5, and from x = 1.5 to x = 4.5. Under the middle of each arrow, at (-3.0, -0.7), (0.0, -0.7) and (3.0, -0.7), write in INK the stacked fraction 3 over 4 followed by the letter m. Below the arrows draw one ANSWER bracket at y = -1.5 from x = -4.5 to x = 4.5: a horizontal line with a short tick at each end pointing up. Centred under the bracket at (0.0, -2.1) write in ANSWER the stacked fraction 9 over 4 followed by the letter m. Neighbouring saplings are exactly 3.0 canvas units apart. Nothing else is drawn: no title, no question words, no ground texture, no people.
must_not_show: a fifth sapling or any gap other than the 3 between four saplings
accuracy_checks: exactly 4 saplings and exactly 3 gaps between the first and the last
each gap is labelled 3/4 m and the 4 sapling x positions differ by exactly 3.0 canvas units
3 x 3/4 = 9/4 m, so the total bracket from the first to the last sapling is labelled 9/4 m
the total bracket starts at the first stem (x = -4.5) and ends at the last stem (x = 4.5)
